summary_paragraph: A 70-year-old woman with a history of severe osteoporosis, prior CABG, and recurrent UTIs was admitted for worsening suprapubic abdominal pain and urinary frequency. She had recently completed a course of ciprofloxacin but reported persistent pain, prompting her to call EMS. Initial evaluation showed pyuria and elevated creatinine at 1.6, indicating acute kidney injury. Urine culture revealed polymicrobial flora, suggesting contamination rather than true infection, so antibiotics were discontinued. Imaging showed stable T12 and lumbar compression fractures with no new spinal changes, and renal ultrasound was normal. Her pain improved without specific intervention, and creatinine decreased to 1.4 by discharge. She remained on her home medications, including tramadol for pain, and was discharged home with instructions to follow up with her primary care provider for repeat labs and osteoporosis management.
